title: Lesson Plan — Linear Equations (Class 10 NIOS Mathematics)
subject: Mathematics
objectives: Identify a linear equation in one or two variables and write it in standard form.
Solve a linear equation in one variable using the equality properties (clearing denominators, distributing, isolating x).
Translate one-unknown word problems (number, age, geometry) into linear equations and solve.
Recognise that a linear equation in two variables has infinitely many solutions, and graph it as a line.
Use the coefficient-ratio test to classify a 2×2 linear system as having unique / no / infinitely many solutions.
Solve a 2×2 linear system by substitution, elimination or cross-multiplication.
prerequisites: Distributive law and the laws of exponents (Chapters 2-3).
Comfort with signed-number arithmetic and fractions.
Plotting points in the Cartesian plane (Class 9).
materials: Cards labelled with assorted equations (linear / non-linear) for a quick-sort starter
Pre-printed table of the three system-classification cases (one per pair)

activities.description: Quick-sort starter. Distribute index cards (3x = 12, x^2 + 1 = 0, x + y = 5, 1/x = 4, 2x − 7 = 3, 4x − 5y = 10). Students sort into 'linear', 'not linear' piles. Take three groups' classifications; reconcile disagreements; promise the rules in Explain phase.
teacher_actions: Listen for disagreements on 1/x and x^2 + 1.

activities.description: Graphing exploration. Students plot the line y = 2x + 1 by picking three x-values and computing y. They then pick a fourth point (x, y) NOT on the line and verify it does not satisfy the equation.
teacher_actions: Use one student's graph as the demo for Explain.
student_actions: Plot three solutions; draw the line.
Pick a non-solution; verify it fails the equation.

activities.description: Direct instruction in four blocks: (i) standard form ax + b = 0; the four equality properties; the 5-step solving plan; worked example 3(x − 2) + 4 = 2x + 1 → x = 3; (ii) word-problem routine with the consecutive-odd integers example; (iii) two-variable equation, infinitely many solutions, graphing as a line; (iv) 2×2 systems, the three cases, and the substitution + elimination methods (with one worked example each).
teacher_actions: Write the 5-step plan on the board.
Use the graph from Explore to motivate 'two equations needed for a unique pair'.
Drill the ratio test with three quick examples.
student_actions: Take notes; replicate every worked example.
Predict the next step before the teacher writes it.
Add the 5-step plan to a 'rules box' for quick reference.

activities.description: Application station. Students work through six worksheet problems: one one-variable solve with denominators; one age word problem; one ratio-test classification; one substitution; one elimination; one cross-multiplication.
teacher_actions: Circulate; offer the smallest hint that unblocks a student.
Collect common slips for the Evaluate phase.
Pair fast finishers with peers who need support.
student_actions: Self-check against a posted answer key.
Verify each by substitution or by the ratio test.

activities.description: Exit-ticket quiz: 8 questions drawn from the chapter's question bank — at least one per outcome. Students complete silently in 9 minutes; project the answers; 4-minute discussion of the two items most missed.
teacher_actions: Distribute exit ticket; remind students it is individual.
Tally; address top two miss items.
student_actions: Self-mark and write a one-line reflection.

activities.description: Set homework: rest of the worksheet, plus one CREATE prompt — 'Write a 2×2 linear system that models a real-life situation involving prices of two items, and solve it.' Preview the next chapter (Quadratic Equations) by writing x^2 − 5x + 6 = 0 on the board and noting that this is what we get when 'linear' is upgraded to 'quadratic' on the variable.
teacher_actions: Bridge to next chapter with the quadratic example.

homework: Complete the remaining problems on the Worksheet — Linear Equations handout.
Construct your own real-life two-variable linear system (prices of two items) and solve it.
Find the value of k for which the system 2x + 3y = 7, kx + 9y = 21 has infinitely many solutions; justify.
assessment_ideas: Use the 8-item exit ticket as a quick formative check.
Set a 12-question quiz drawn from the chapter's question bank for the next class as a summative assessment.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on the boat-and-current word problem using the auto-grade rubric.
Run a 5-minute peer-grading round on the CREATE homework using a two-criterion rubric (system makes sense? solution verified?).
references: NIOS Secondary Mathematics, Module 1, Lesson 5: Linear Equations.
NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 3: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables (parallel coverage).
